questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Language learning and exploring new cultures. Making friends abroad.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The language spoken at the destination. My main goal was to improve my spanish. 
Recommendations from other students. 
Beautiful landscape with great hiking possibilities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Awesome experience that I would recommend to anyone considering going! Fantastic local ESN (erasmus student network) volunteers that are so helpful and friendly, arranging all kinds of social events. Very kind, open and friendly hospital staff. 
Only negative is that you have to be patient when arranging your hospital stay and trust that it will all be fixed once you arrive.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got a mail stating where I should go the first day for the introduction. I was received by Beatriz who gave me some introduction and told me where to get my uniform and where to go at the hospital. Very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Read above.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Remember that the hospital is in Gijón and not Oviedo!!
I used “
Idealista.com
” to find a flat in Gijón (el Llano). There is also a whatsapp group for erasmus students you can join. You can find it by writing to the instagram “esnoviedo” and ask them to add you. It started looking a week before arriving and found something pretty quickly. I would recommend looking sooner though.
And dont sign a contract before seing the flat first!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It’s what everyone does and its a lot cheaper. Most erasmus students live together in shared flats paying around 300 euros a month.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only heard bad things about the housing offered by the university so find something on your own in Gijón.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did everything from home just following the instructions from the e-mails. When I arrived I didnt have to do anything.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just applyed through KU-net and followed the steps on mobility online. I also got some e-mails from University of Oviedo asking me to register online. KU were very helpful with the learning agreement.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote to Anne Fledelius a number of times and she was very helpful with everything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not relevant as I just did the internship at the hospital.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience. Everything will sort itself out in time. They are very chill and laid back and you can solve the details and what departments you will be at in the hospital once you arrive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Very kind and open staff, both doctors, nurses etc. Very patient and curious. Eager to explain stuff and let you be active if you ask to, especially in anaesthesia. 
I love the equal and non-hierarchy mentality that they have in Spain. You can always ask questions and crack jokes even with the senior doctors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took the masters course “ophold ved udenlandsk universitetshospital.”

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a clinical stay of 13 weeks. I did not have any classes or exams. Apart from that its much like the clinical stays in Denmark, maybe a bit less organised.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: “Ophold ved udenlandsk universitetshospital” / “stay at foreign university hospital”

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
“Stay at foreign university hospital”
For all the reasons mentioned above.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I payed extra to have my own flat because my parents and my girlfriend came to visit me, so dont expect to pay that much.
Public transportation is very good and cheap. Especially if you go to the “ayuntamiento” and get the citizens card.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
This was the best part of the trip. Football (soccer) and volleyball every tuesday and thursday for the erasmus students. Free fitness center and all kinds of facilities I didnt use. 
Such a good way to get to know people.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Football and volley every tuesday and thursday. Tapas night every tuesday and thursday after sports. Theme parties every friday. Trekking/hiking trips. Trips to other places like León or Gilicia, even a trip to Ibiza. 
Kayaking trips. Trips to local festivals and concerts, traditional food trips and picnics, international dinners where everyone brings traditional food from their home country. And much more!

All arranged by the ESN volunteers. Find them on instagram (esnoviedo) and join the whatsapp group.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Everything mentioned above depending on your interests.
Go to “Tierra astur” to eat!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Los picos de Europa. La ruta de cares. Beautiful trekking routes.
Also “playa de la ñora” is a fantastic beach. You can trek from Gijón. 
I also liked León, Bilbao and San Sebastián.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: You have to get used to things not being as organised as in Denmark. They compensate by being very open and solve every problem in the moment.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Follow the esnoviedo instagram and join the whatsapp groups. I also joined a climbing gym and got some friends there. Its very easy as everyone is very open and talkative.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Lunch at 15 and dinner at 22. I had some snacks in my pocket at the hospital. Everyone comes 1h late to everything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The openness, friendlines and curiosity. I love that people actually talk to strangers in the streets, on the bus and in stores. You feel very welcomed, its easy to get new friends and people are very curious about your culture and situation.  
The food is amazing!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Follow esnoviedo on instagram and join the whatsapp group.

Practice some spanish before coming (universidad de oviedo also offers cheap classes in jan-feb at casa de las lenguas) as everything is in spanish at the hospital. 

Be patient with the application process and getting your clinical stays confirmed. I sorted it out the last things when I arrived and it was so much easier. Also pick anaesthesia, they let you intubate and do spinal anaesthesia.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing else.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Getting friends from across the world. Being able to attend patients in spanish. Feeling fluent in spanish and having spanish speaking friends. 

My friends an family visiting me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Being away from my girlfriend for 3 months. 
Not understanding everything that was going on at first. This became better as I improved my spanish.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
If you are considering going, just do it! 
And remember to be proactive at the hospital. Many times if you just ask they will let you do and practice stuff.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
